paras.text: 2. Provision of developmental finance (Provision of Developmental Finance)
paras.urdu: 2۔ ترقیاتی مالیات کی بہم رسانی (Provision of Developmental Finance):
paras.pashto: ۲. د پراختیايي مالیې برابرول (Provision of Developmental Finance)

paras.text: In 1956 the State Bank of Pakistan Order 1948 was changed into the State Bank of Pakistan Act, by virtue of which the purposes of the bank were determined afresh, and this responsibility was placed on it, that the monetary and credit system of the country be made regular, so that on the one hand monetary stability may be created and on the other hand full benefit may be taken from the productive resources of the country. After that many amendments were made in this Act, from which the bank was made capable of taking part effectively, by providing medium- and long-term finance, in the efforts being made to develop the economy. By an amendment of 1970 in the “State Bank Act” this bank can buy the bills and debentures, i.e. loan bonds (Debenture), of any public company or corporation, can discount them, or can keep them in its custody. In short, the State Bank has made the banking and credit system of the country stronger, so that loans can be provided for developmental purposes. At this time there are eight institutions providing development finance.

paras.urdu: 4۔ قرضوں کی متوازن تقسیم (Balanced Distribution of Credit):

2. Provision of developmental finance (Provision of Developmental Finance)

In 1956 the State Bank of Pakistan Order 1948 was changed into the State Bank of Pakistan Act, by virtue of which the purposes of the bank were determined afresh, and this responsibility was placed on it, that the monetary and credit system of the country be made regular, so that on the one hand monetary stability may be created and on the other hand full benefit may be taken from the productive resources of the country. After that many amendments were made in this Act, from which the bank was made capable of taking part effectively, by providing medium- and long-term finance, in the efforts being made to develop the economy. By an amendment of 1970 in the “State Bank Act” this bank can buy the bills and debentures, i.e. loan bonds (Debenture), of any public company or corporation, can discount them, or can keep them in its custody. In short, the State Bank has made the banking and credit system of the country stronger, so that loans can be provided for developmental purposes. At this time there are eight institutions providing development finance.

3. Help of special credit institutions (Special Financial Institutions)

The State Bank has provided reasonable funds to special financial institutions; e.g. to speed up the pace of development of the agricultural sector, the State Bank has given large amounts to institutions of mutual aid and has increased the resources of the Zarai Taraqiati Bank. By buying the debentures of the House Building Finance Corporation it has increased its financial resources too. To create ease in the work of selling within the country the machinery made locally, the State Bank sanctioned loans to special financial institutions.

4. Balanced distribution of credit (Balanced Distribution of Credit)

In view of the demands of the national economy, the State Bank, in order to make its policies of giving loans successful, makes ordinary banks ready through moral persuasion, selective credit control and other measures. Thus because of these measures the patterns of giving loans of banks have changed; e.g. in June 1954 sixty per cent of the total bank credit was given to the commercial sector, eighteen per cent to the industrial sector and twenty-two per cent to the remaining sectors. Whereas at this time the share of the commercial sector, decreasing, has remained approximately 30 per cent, that of the industrial sector, increasing, 40 per cent, and the share of other sectors has become 30 per cent.

5. Monetary stability and credit control measures (remedy of inflation)

Among the big responsibilities of the State Bank, one important responsibility is this, that it organise the monetary and credit system of the country, so that monetary stability can be created in Pakistan. By monetary stability is meant that protection be made from inflation and deflation (i.e. decrease in the quantity of money), and moderation and balance be kept in the accounts of external payments. For this purpose the most important condition is this, that the supply of money be so regulated that balance remains maintained between “aggregate purchasing power” (Aggregate Purchasing Power) and “supply of goods and services” (Supply of Goods & Services).

To stop inflation the State Bank has made the “structure of interest rates” such that from it, on the one hand, productive sectors get an impetus for development, and on the other hand loans for “unproductive” and speculative (Speculative) purposes are discouraged. 2۔ ترقیاتی مالیات کی بہم رسانی (Provision of Developmental Finance):

1956ء میں سٹیٹ بینک آف پاکستان آرڈر 1948ء کو سٹیٹ بینک آف پاکستان ایکٹ میں بدل دیا گیا۔ جس کی بدولت بینک کے مقاصد کو از سرِ نو متعین کیا گیا اور اس پر یہ ذمہ داری ڈال دی گئی کہ ملک کے زری اور کریڈٹ نظام کو باقاعدہ بنایا جائے تاکہ ایک طرف زری استحکام پیدا ہو اور دوسری طرف ملک کے پیداواری وسائل سے پورا پورا فائدہ اٹھایا جا سکے۔ بعد ازاں اس ایکٹ میں کئی ترمیمات کی گئیں جن سے بینک کو اس قابل بنایا گیا کہ اوسط اور طویل مدت مالیات مہیا کر کے معیشت کو ترقی دینے کی جو کوششیں کی جا رہی ہیں، ان میں یہ موثر انداز سے شرکت کر سکے۔ ”سٹیٹ بینک ایکٹ“ میں 1970ء کی ایک ترمیم کے ذریعے یہ بینک کسی بھی پبلک کمپنی یا کارپوریشن کی ہنڈیاں اور ڈبینچر یعنی قرضہ کی سند یا دینیہ (Debenture) خرید سکتا ہے، ان پر بٹہ لگا سکتا ہے، یا اپنی تحویل میں رکھ سکتا ہے۔ غرض سٹیٹ بینک نے ملک کے بینک اور کریڈٹ نظام کو مضبوط تر بنایا ہے، تاکہ ترقیاتی مقاصد کے لئے قرضہ مہیا کیا جا سکے۔ اس وقت ترقیاتی مالیت مہیا کرنے والے آٹھ ادارے ہیں۔

3۔ خصوصی قرضہ جاتی اداروں (Special Financial Institutions) کی امداد:

سٹیٹ بینک نے خصوصی مالی اداروں کو معقول فنڈ مہیا کئے ہیں۔ مثلاً زرعی شعبہ کی رفتارِ ترقی تیز کرنے کے لئے سٹیٹ بینک نے امدادِ باہمی کے اداروں کو کثیر رقمیں دی ہیں اور زرعی ترقیاتی بینک کے وسائل میں اضافہ کیا ہے۔ مکان تعمیر کرنے کی مالی کارپوریشن کے ڈبینچر خرید کر اس کے مالی وسائل کو بھی بڑھایا ہے۔ مقامی طور پر بننے والی مشینری کی ملک کے اندر فروخت کے کام میں سہولت پیدا کرنے کے لئے سٹیٹ بینک نے خصوصی مالی اداروں کو قرضہ منظور کیا۔

4۔ قرضوں کی متوازن تقسیم (Balanced Distribution of Credit):

ملکی معیشت کے تقاضوں کے پیشِ نظر سٹیٹ بینک اپنی قرضہ دینے کی پالیسیوں کو کامیاب بنانے کے لئے عام بینکوں کو اخلاقی ترغیبات، انتخابی کریڈٹ کنٹرول اور دیگر اقدامات کے ذریعے مستعد بناتا ہے۔ چنانچہ ان اقدامات کی وجہ سے بینکوں کے قرضہ دینے کے انداز بدل گئے ہیں۔ مثلاً جون 1954ء میں کل بینک کریڈٹ کا ساٹھ فی صد حصہ تجارتی شعبے کو دیا گیا، اٹھارہ فیصد صنعتی شعبے کو اور بیس فیصد باقی شعبوں کو۔ جب کہ اس وقت تجارتی شعبے کا حصہ کم ہو کر تقریباً 30 فیصد رہ گیا ہے، صنعتی شعبے کا بڑھ کر 40 فیصد اور دیگر شعبوں کا حصہ 30 فیصد ہو گیا ہے۔

5۔ زری استحکام اور کریڈٹ کنٹرول اقدامات (افراطِ زر کا علاج):

سٹیٹ بینک کی بڑی بڑی ذمہ داریوں میں سے ایک اہم ذمہ داری یہ ہے کہ ملک کا زری اور کریڈٹ نظام منظم کرے، تاکہ پاکستان میں زری استحکام پیدا کیا جا سکے۔ زری استحکام سے مراد یہ ہے کہ افراطِ زر اور تفریطِ زر (یعنی زر کی مقدار میں کمی) سے بچاؤ کیا جائے اور بیرونی ادائیگیوں کے حسابات میں اعتدال و توازن رکھا جائے۔ اس مقصد کے لئے اہم ترین شرط یہ ہے کہ زر کی رسد کو یوں باقاعدہ بنایا جائے کہ ”مجموعی قوتِ خرید“ (Aggregate Purchasing Power) اور ”اشیاء و خدمات کی رسد“ (Supply of Goods & Services) میں توازن برقرار رہے۔

افراطِ زر کو روکنے کے لئے سٹیٹ بینک نے ”شرح سود کا ڈھانچہ“ ایسا بنایا ہوا ہے جس سے ایک طرف پیداواری شعبوں کو ترقی کی تحریک ملتی ہے اور دوسری طرف ”غیر پیداواری“ اور تخمینی (Speculative) مقاصد کے لئے قرضہ کی حوصلہ شکنی ہوتی ہے۔ سٹیٹ بینک مذکورہ ”مقداری کریڈٹ کنٹرول“ اقدامات کے علاوہ صفاتی یا ”انتخابی کریڈٹ کنٹرول“ کے طریقے بھی استعمال کرتا ہے۔ پہلی قسم کے …

paras.text: 6. Prevention of concentration of credit
paras.urdu: 6۔ قرضہ کے ارتکاز کا سدِباب:
paras.pashto: ۶. د پور د تمرکز مخنیوی

paras.text: After the establishment of Pakistan, in the “strategy” of economic development that was adopted for the first twenty years, much emphasis was laid on this point, that the pace of economic development be made fast. In this connection the aspects of “social justice” (Social Justice) and distribution of wealth were completely ignored, the result of which emerged that economic wealth and power became concentrated (Concentrate) in a few hands. In these conditions the concentration of bank credit too with a few institutions was a natural matter. Therefore the State Bank took many measures to reduce this concentration and to spread the facilities of loans on a wide scale. The State Bank fixed targets (Target) for commercial banks for giving loans to small business people, and along with them also fixed “upper limits”, beyond which more loan cannot be given to ordinary people, directors of banks, public limited companies and bank employees.
paras.urdu: پاکستان کے قیام کے بعد پہلے بیس سال تک معاشی ترقی کی ”جو حکمتِ عملی“ اختیار کی گئی، اس میں اس بات پر بہت زور دیا گیا کہ اقتصادی ترقی کی رفتار تیز کر دی جائے اس ضمن میں ”معاشرتی انصاف“ (Social Justice) اور تقسیمِ دولت کے پہلوؤں کو بالکل نظر انداز کر دیا گیا، جس کا یہ نتیجہ نکلا کہ معاشی دولت اور قوت چند ہاتھوں میں مرتکز (Concentrate) ہو کر رہ گئی۔ ان حالات میں بینک کریڈٹ کا بھی چند اداروں کے پاس مرتکز ہو جانا قدرتی امر تھا۔ لہٰذا سٹیٹ بینک نے اس ارتکاز کو کم کرنے اور قرضے کی سہولتوں کو وسیع پیمانے پر پھیلانے کے لئے کئی اقدامات کئے۔ سٹیٹ بینک نے تجارتی بینکوں کو چھوٹے کاروباری لوگوں کو قرضے دینے کے ہدف (Target) مقرر کر دیئے اور ساتھ ہی ”بالائی حدیں“ بھی مقرر کر دیں۔ جن سے زیادہ قرضہ عام لوگوں، بینکوں کے ڈائریکٹروں، پبلک لمیٹڈ کمپنیوں اور بینک ملازموں کو نہیں دیا جا سکتا۔

paras.text: 7. Small Business Division (department of small business)

6. Prevention of concentration of credit

After the establishment of Pakistan, in the “strategy” of economic development that was adopted for the first twenty years, much emphasis was laid on this point, that the pace of economic development be made fast. In this connection the aspects of “social justice” (Social Justice) and distribution of wealth were completely ignored, the result of which emerged that economic wealth and power became concentrated (Concentrate) in a few hands. In these conditions the concentration of bank credit too with a few institutions was a natural matter. Therefore the State Bank took many measures to reduce this concentration and to spread the facilities of loans on a wide scale. The State Bank fixed targets (Target) for commercial banks for giving loans to small business people, and along with them also fixed “upper limits”, beyond which more loan cannot be given to ordinary people, directors of banks, public limited companies and bank employees.

From them a fair degree of stability and steadiness can be created in the prices of particular goods. The State Bank also has this authority, that it can issue instructions to banks about the following matters: volume of credit, prevailing rate of interest on deposits and loans, credit policy and investment policy.

In November 1997 the State Bank issued detailed instructions that no banking company in Pakistan can continue the business of banking until its minimum paid-up capital (Paid Up Capital) is one billion (arab) rupees, and until its reserves (Reserves) are not equal to eight per cent of its risk-weighted assets (Risk Weighted Assets).

6. Prevention of concentration of credit

After the establishment of Pakistan, in the “strategy” of economic development that was adopted for the first twenty years, much emphasis was laid on this point, that the pace of economic development be made fast. In this connection the aspects of “social justice” (Social Justice) and distribution of wealth were completely ignored, the result of which emerged that economic wealth and power became concentrated (Concentrate) in a few hands. In these conditions the concentration of bank credit too with a few institutions was a natural matter. Therefore the State Bank took many measures to reduce this concentration and to spread the facilities of loans on a wide scale. The State Bank fixed targets (Target) for commercial banks for giving loans to small business people, and along with them also fixed “upper limits”, beyond which more loan cannot be given to ordinary people, directors of banks, public limited companies and bank employees.

7. Small Business Division (department of small business)

The State Bank has established a “Small Business Division”, whose work is this, that it review the problems of small business people, and supervise this thing, that the limit which has been fixed for issuing small loans is being acted upon.

8. Export finance scheme

Under this scheme loans are given to exporting traders in connection with exporting goods from Pakistan. It has two parts: under the first part loans are given to traders on showing an irrevocable letter of credit (L.C.) or on receiving a firm order for exporting goods. Under the second part, while fixing the limit of the loan to be given for exports, the export performance of the past year is seen.

9. Training of banking staff (Training of Bank Staff)

The training department of the State Bank gives technical training to bank officers. To give “in-service” training within the country, the bank has established two training institutions: one in Karachi and the other in Lahore.

10. Coordination board

In February 1994 the bank, by an amendment in its State Bank of Pakistan Act 1956, established a “Monetary and Fiscal Policies Coordination Board” (The Monetary and Fiscal Policies Coordination Board), whose president is the federal finance minister, and its members are these: the federal commerce minister, the deputy chairman of the Planning Commission, the governor of the State Bank and the federal finance secretary.
